report_title: Decimal scalar loops and u8 and i8 parser adaptations
selected_scope_from_report:
For every byte slice, the adapted standard decimal complete and partial u8 and
i8 parsers return the specified value or error, including sign handling, the
first overflow, underflow, or invalid-byte position, and the consumed count in partial mode.
The signed contracts account for the asymmetric i8 limits. The checked u32 and
u8 scalar loops allow arbitrary initial accumulators; the positive and negative
i32 loops require nonnegative and nonpositive initial accumulators, respectively.
Cursor-based loops require cursor plus remaining length to fit in usize. The
unchecked u8 loop is covered starting at zero with at most two bytes. Separately,
lexical-util's extracted char_to_digit_const returns the specified ASCII digit
option for every byte and radix from 2 through 36.
limitations_from_report:
The parser mappings concern harness adaptations, not the original generic
release parser. The scalar loops outline the release macro and replace its
iterator with slices; a source checker checks the specified loop transformations.
The selected front ends and iterator adaptation were separately reviewed.
Neither source comparison nor review is a formal Rust-to-Rust equivalence proof.
Other widths and formats and block fast-path integration are outside these front-end
theorems. The digit conversion mapping concerns the extracted lexical-util body.
